name: Vancouver, BC
summary: Vancouver is a strong all-rounder: a flat, walkable downtown and West End by False Creek, Stanley Park and English Bay, dozens of restaurants on foot, two public courses within 40 minutes, typical July highs around 73 F, and nonstop flights from Denver and SFO. Provincial and city short-term rental rules leave no legal whole house with a guest suite in the city, so the workable setup is three separate suites in one apartment hotel. The best bookable one is Level Yaletown-Seymour, verified at US$1,401-1,796/night for Jul 4-10 with a pool and hot tub; Carmana Hotel & Suites downtown is verified at US$1,413/night and gives the teens twin beds; La Grande Residence is verified at US$1,755. Each household gets its own door, but no room seats all 8 at one table. The biggest caveat is animals: the two hands-on options are farm animals about 55 minutes away (a horseback trail ride in Langley, Tue-Sun, and alpaca feeding and walks, Fri-Sun), with a Deep Cove kayak paddle among harbour seals as the best wildlife outing; the Aquarium seal encounter is 14+ and the sea otter encounter is sold out indefinitely. Passports are required.

hard_constraints.notes: Airport: YVR is about 30 min by car from downtown (Canada Line train also runs to Yaletown-Roundhouse and Waterfront); nonstops from DEN (United, Air Canada) and SFO, so it passes. Seniors: the recommended Level Yaletown-Seymour is a high-rise at 1022 Seymour St (elevator not stated in the listings read, but suites above ground level are reached by lift in a tower this size; confirm); Granville St restaurants are 1-3 min and Yaletown's Hamilton/Mainland streets 5-8 min on flat sidewalks, the False Creek seawall about 10 min. The West End options (Lord Stanley Suites; backup Times Square Suites) are flatter still to English Bay and Stanley Park. Capilano and Grouse involve stairs and trails, but those are optional for the parents. Passes.

rationale.lodging: 15/25: rests on Level Yaletown-Seymour (two 1BR suites + a Deluxe 2BR/2BA, US$1,401-1,796/night, verified for Jul 4-10, re-quoted 2026-11-15): each household has its own suite and kitchen and the building has a pool and hot tub, but no private room seats all 8 at a table and the 2BR's two queens leave the teens sharing a bed or the sofa bed.
rationale.town_scenery: 15/18: downtown, Yaletown and the West End are flat and walkable to the False Creek and Stanley Park seawalls with water and mountain views, but it is a big city, not a village.
rationale.animals: 8/18: ranked by what guests do, the top items are a Deep Cove kayak paddle among harbour seals (25 min, 12+, sightings not guaranteed, not for the parents) and a guided horseback trail ride at Glen Valley Stables (about 55 min, 6+, Tue-Sun), then alpaca feeding and walks at Kensington Prairie Farm (55 min, Fri-Sun); the only hands-on options are farm animals, which keeps the category in the lower half; whale watching (2027 dates unconfirmed) and the Grouse grizzly add viewing, and the Aquarium seal encounter (14+, excludes Aubrey) and the sold-out sea otter encounter do not count.
rationale.food: 15/15: more than 10 restaurants within an 8-minute flat walk of Level Seymour on Granville St and in Yaletown (Destination Vancouver lists 20 in Yaletown), with Blue Water Cafe about 6 minutes away for the special dinner.
rationale.other: 9/10: Capilano bridges, seawall bikes, an outdoor escape game, Granville Island shopping and Science World cover teens, parents and rain; DEN and SFO nonstops and a 30-min transfer, with passports needed.
rationale.golf: 7/9: Furry Creek on Howe Sound (about 40 min) is the scenic pick, University Golf Club (20 min) the alternative; July green fees are unconfirmed and University GC is mid-renovation.
rationale.weather: 5/5: July normal high about 73 F (at or under the 75 F target) with about 7 rain days.

animals.name: Deep Cove Kayak Centre: Deep Cove Explorer tour (harbour seals)
animals.what_you_do: Paddle a guided 3-hour kayak tour through the south end of Indian Arm, where the operator says harbour seals are abundant, along with eagles and sea stars; sightings are not guaranteed.
animals.why_memorable: Kayaking among wild harbour seals in a mountain fjord, 25 minutes from downtown, with Deep Cove's doughnut shop at the dock.
animals.price_usd: C$95 per person plus GST and a C$1 transaction fee (operator page; 2027 rate not stated)
animals.booking_difficulty: Book online or call 604.929.2268. Runs daily March-November, rain or shine; July-August departures 9-12, 1-4 and 5-8. Under-16s must share a double kayak with an adult 1:1 (Ethan and Aubrey each with a parent). Not for Sam and Karen.

animals.name: Glen Valley Stables guided trail rides, Campbell Valley Park
animals.what_you_do: Ride a horse with a guide through Campbell Valley Park in Langley on a 1-hour, 1.5-hour or 2-hour trail ride; groups of 6+ get a private ride at the group rate.
animals.why_memorable: The fullest hands-on animal activity near Vancouver, open to first-time riders and to everyone 6 and up, so Ethan and Aubrey can ride with the adults.
animals.price_usd: 2025 rates plus 5% GST: group C$95 (1 hr), C$145 (1.5 hr), C$180 (2 hr) per person; private C$130-215 per person (min 2); 2027 rates not published
animals.booking_difficulty: Rates page states 6+ only in its Birthday Rides section; confirm it applies to all rides. Book by call or text (778-710-1941). Open Tue-Sun year-round, closed Mondays (open holiday Mondays), weather permitting; rain-cancelled rides rescheduled free. Weight limit not stated. Riding is not suited to the parents.

animals.name: Kensington Prairie Farm alpaca walks and meet + greets
animals.what_you_do: Feed and lead an alpaca on a 30-min walk, or feed and visit alpacas in their pen; farm tours also include feeding alpacas and llamas.
animals.why_memorable: Feeding and walking alpacas suits Aubrey and Andrea, and the pen visit works for the parents too.
animals.price_usd: Walk C$105 per alpaca (2 people max); Meet + Greet C$200 per group of 5; farm tour C$25 pp; admission C$7.50
animals.booking_difficulty: Pre-booking required. Farm open Fri 12-5, Sat 10-4, Sun 12-4 only (closed Mon-Thu), so Fri Jul 9 is the realistic day; walk and meet + greet times are not listed separately, and no age minimum or 2027 schedule is stated.
